title: Sub-Scope Report Customisation Architecture
summary: reference the shared docs_subscope report, registered customisations, generated data, exact action targets, browser composition, and extension checks
content_html:
Sub-Scope Report Customisation Architecture

Purpose

This document is the implementation reference for extending a configured one-level sub-scope report. It defines the shared default, the registered customisation seam, the generated-data contract, browser composition, exact targets, public isolation, failure behaviour, and the checks required when a new customisation is added.

The governing rule is:

configured sub-scope
  -> generated manifest and by-ID records
  -> docs_subscope report engine
  -> public-safe shared behaviour
  -> Manage default contribution
  -> optional registered access-specific customisation

The customisation is an explicit property of the configured collection. It is not inferred from scope, sub_scope, a filename, a title, or a special case inside the shared report.

Choose The Smallest Extension Point

Use the existing docs_subscope default when a collection needs the standard flat list/detail reader and standard Manage document actions.

Add a registered customisation when the collection needs additive behaviour such as:

  • projected collection or row metadata;
  • another list filter;
  • row decoration or an additional column;
  • an additional collection, selection, or validated-detail action; or
  • collection-specific lifecycle observation.

Add a different report engine only when the collection has fundamentally different membership, navigation, or detail semantics. Do not add scope/sub-scope branches to the shared engine or make a customisation replace its core list, detail, validation, and navigation ownership.

Identity And Report Host

The collection target is exactly:

{"scope": "<scope-id>", "sub_scope": "<sub-scope-id>"}

A child-document target is exactly:

{
  "scope": "<scope-id>",
  "sub_scope": "<sub-scope-id>",
  "doc_id": "<document-id>"
}

The indexed parent report host is an ordinary parent-scope document with:

viewer_report: docs_subscope
viewer_report_access: local
viewer_report_subscope: <sub-scope-id>

The host selects the report engine and exact collection. The configured sub-scope record selects the customisation. Config must not contain a module path or executable name.

New sub-scopes receive this parent report host through the normal sub-scope lifecycle. Child documents remain excluded from parent Index, Recent, and search results; the indexed host is their durable entry point.

Configuration Contract

No report_customisation field means the canonical default:

{
  "sub_scope": "default",
  "title": "Default",
  "ui_statuses": ["draft", "done"],
  "public_projection": null
}

A customisation record has exactly id and settings:

{
  "sub_scope": "tags",
  "title": "Tags",
  "public_title": "Concepts",
  "report_customisation": {
    "id": "analysis_tags",
    "settings": {
      "groups": ["subject", "domain", "form", "theme"]
    }
  }
}

Customisation IDs match [a-z][a-z0-9_]*. The Python registry validates the ID and owns the exact settings schema. Unknown IDs, unknown fields, missing fields, and invalid settings fail configuration loading.

Settings are server-side input. Browser config exposes only report_customisation: {"id": "..."} for an access level that has a registered browser implementation. Browser code consumes projected manifest data, not raw settings.

Canonical Default

The shared public-safe engine owns:

  • configured collection validation and complete manifest membership;
  • list, detail, empty, unavailable, invalid, and contained error states;
  • NFKC-normalized case-insensitive title-prefix search;
  • deterministic title-ascending or last_updated-descending order;
  • by-ID payload loading and document identity validation;
  • subdoc URL navigation and browser history; and
  • the clean absence of management controls in public access.

The recency order puts missing or invalid timestamps after dated documents, then uses title and doc_id as stable tie-breakers.

The Manage default contribution adds:

  • status and non-viewable presentation from the compact Manage manifest row;
  • collection-local checkbox selection;
  • Select all, Clear, and Done selection controls;
  • exact-collection New document, including for an empty collection;
  • checked-ID Prepare Package;
  • validated-detail Copy Link and Delete; and
  • publication of the mounted exact collection or detail for the app-level Import owner.

Changing sort or filters does not rewrite checked IDs. Select all and Shift-range operate on the current visible sorted projection. Copy Link produces a Markdown link to the exact report host URL with subdoc; it does not copy a source or management-service URL.

Import is an app-level action. It consumes the exact collection published by the mounted report and is not registered as a report-toolbar action.

Customisations add to these behaviours. They do not remove, replace, or clear the default contribution.

Generated Data Contract

The builder owns the manifest, by-ID records, and browser route values. The browser does not discover membership from source folders.

The public manifest contains viewable documents only:

{
  "docs": [
    {"doc_id": "d-example", "title": "Example"}
  ]
}

The Manage manifest contains every collection document with compact lifecycle metadata:

{
  "docs": [
    {
      "doc_id": "d-example",
      "title": "Example",
      "ui_status": "draft",
      "viewable": false,
      "last_updated": "2026-08-01 08:00:00"
    }
  ]
}

An access-enabled customisation may add a strict root namespace and per-row data:

{
  "docs": [
    {
      "doc_id": "d-example",
      "title": "Example",
      "customisation": {"group": "subject"}
    }
  ],
  "customisation": {
    "id": "analysis_tags",
    "data": {"groups": ["subject", "domain", "form", "theme"]}
  }
}

Projection rules are strict:

  • the descriptor ID and manifest customisation ID must match exactly;
  • custom row data may target only a document already in that manifest;
  • custom data cannot collide with builder-owned fields;
  • invalid custom values fail the build;
  • no configured customisation produces no custom namespace; and
  • an empty collection still produces a valid empty manifest and report.

Public data is generated at the configured public_projection. Manage data is generated with the working scope. External-local Manage routes use /docs/published/external/<scope>/<sub_scope>; consumers use generated browser config rather than constructing either route.

Registration And Access

Registration is explicit on both sides of the build/browser boundary.

The Python definition supplies:

  • customisation_id;
  • normalize_settings;
  • optional document_groups metadata support;
  • public_browser access; and
  • manage_browser access.

project_report_customisation_manifest() owns the allowed manifest projection for the ID. A new projector must be added to its controlled dispatch; config must never name a projector.

Each enabled browser access needs a lazy loader with the same ID:

  • public loaders live in site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-subscope-customisation-registry.js;
  • Manage loaders live in docs-viewer/runtime/js/management/docs-viewer-management-subscope-customisation-registry.js.

The Python access registry and JavaScript loader registries are tested for exact agreement. At present analysis_tags is Manage-only and the public loader registry is intentionally empty.

An absent descriptor resolves to the default. An unknown descriptor, missing loader, invalid factory, descriptor/manifest mismatch, or callback failure is a contained report error. It must not silently fall back to the default after a customisation was explicitly selected.

Browser Contribution Contract

A browser factory validates its descriptor and returns an object containing only the callbacks it needs:

Callback Use
createFilters(context) Return additive filter descriptors.
renderRow(context) Populate detached leading, title-prefix, or trailing row hosts.
renderListToolbar(context) Add collection or selection controls.
renderSelectionToolbar(context) Add controls tied to the current immutable selection snapshot in Manage.
renderDetailToolbar(context) Add controls only after a by-ID record has been validated.
notify(event) Observe explicit collection-scoped lifecycle events.

The shared report supplies detached contribution hosts. A host enters the DOM only when populated. Manage renders the default owner first and the custom owner second, preserving ownership and CSS boundaries.

renderRow may return accessibleLabels; the engine incorporates them into the row's accessible name. It must not replace the row's document identity or navigation.

A filter descriptor contains a unique id, a boolean-returning matches function, a render function, and optionally initialValue. The render callback receives its host, current value, and setValue. Filters receive the complete normalized records and produce the visible projection only; they do not redefine collection membership.

The current analysis_tags contribution is deliberately small: it reads projected data.groups and row customisation.group, then contributes a group filter. It is not the source of the default report behaviour.

Action, Target, And Refresh Contract

Manage toolbar actions are declared through the supplied registrar. Each definition requires:

Field Contract
id Non-empty action identity.
placement Must match list-toolbar, selection, or detail-toolbar host ownership.
targetKind collection, selection, or validated-detail.
emptyState enabled, disabled, or omitted.
refreshEffect none, collection, open-created-document, or commit-deleted-document.
capability Boolean or {available, reason}; omitted means available.
handler Function accepting the registrar's exact validated target and refresh helpers.

Target resolution is central and has no fallback:

  • collection receives exact {scope, sub_scope};
  • selection receives exact {scope, sub_scope, doc_ids} with a frozen, de-duplicated checked-ID snapshot and is unavailable when it is empty; and
  • validated-detail receives exact {scope, sub_scope, doc_id} only after the manifest and by-ID payload identities agree.

Handlers receive refreshCollection, refreshDocument, and the declared refreshEffect. Creation must refresh and open the committed returned target. Deletion must reconcile the committed exact target. A presentation failure after a successful mutation must retry presentation only; it must not repeat the mutation.

Lifecycle Events

notify(event) receives explicit events scoped to access and collection:

Event Important fields
mount root
refresh complete immutable documents, projected customisation data, reason
projection visible immutable documents, filterValues, sort, reason
selection immutable selection with active, checkedDocIds, and eligibleDocIds, plus reason
state state, nullable validated target, reason, refreshDocument, refreshCollection
unmount reason

Use refresh when logic needs complete collection membership and projection when it needs the current filtered/sorted rows. Do not derive an action target from an event's displayed text, URL, parent document, or current selection unless that exact target is present in the event or action context.

Public And Manage Isolation

The shared report and public registry must remain safe for the published import graph. Public code must not import management modules, management services, or Manage-only customisations.

Access is decided in the Python definition and reflected in browser config, manifest projection, and the matching JavaScript registry. A Manage-only customisation therefore has:

  • no public descriptor;
  • no public custom manifest namespace;
  • no public loader; and
  • no public import edge.

Do not rely on a hidden button or runtime branch as the isolation boundary.

Adding A Customisation

Use this sequence:

  1. Define the collection requirement and confirm that it is additive to the shared membership, list/detail, navigation, and default Manage behaviour.
  2. Choose a stable snake-case ID and an exact settings schema.
  3. Add the Python definition, settings normalization, access flags, optional document metadata choices, and controlled manifest projector.
  4. Add a small browser factory and register a lazy loader only for each enabled access.
  5. Add the sub-scope config record with the registered ID and valid settings.
  6. Rebuild the affected scope and inspect browser config, public/Manage manifests, by-ID records, and the published report host.
  7. Add focused configuration, builder, registry-boundary, module, route, and browser acceptance coverage in proportion to the added surface.

Before considering the extension complete, verify:

  • the collection without a descriptor still uses the unchanged default;
  • malformed config and projection data fail deterministically;
  • browser descriptor and manifest IDs must agree;
  • public and Manage access match the Python registry;
  • empty, populated, filtered, detail, invalid-detail, and error states render;
  • custom content is additive and uses detached owned hosts;
  • every mutation receives an exact target and applies the declared refresh effect; and
  • selection remains collection-local across sort, filters, refresh, and detail navigation.

Current Reference Implementations

studio/default is the default-only reference. It has no customisation descriptor and demonstrates the generic report and standard Manage actions.

analysis/tags is the registered customisation reference. Its Manage manifest projects allowed groups and per-document group values; its Manage factory adds the group filter. Its public Concepts projection remains on the shared default and receives no Manage-only metadata or module.

These examples demonstrate the seam. Neither collection identity should be hard-coded into the shared report.

Code Authority

Concern Authority
Config validation, settings, access, projection dispatch docs-viewer/services/docs_subscope_report_customisations.py
Manifest and by-ID generation docs-viewer/build/docs_builder/sub_scope.py
Browser config projection docs-viewer/build/docs_builder/browser_config.py
Shared list/detail engine and contribution contexts site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-subscope-report.js
Public customisation resolution site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-subscope-customisation-registry.js
Manage customisation resolution docs-viewer/runtime/js/management/docs-viewer-management-subscope-customisation-registry.js
Manage default behaviour docs-viewer/runtime/js/management/docs-viewer-management-subscope-default-contribution.js
Default/custom composition and action registrar docs-viewer/runtime/js/management/docs-viewer-management-subscope-composition.js
Manage report/app integration docs-viewer/runtime/js/management/docs-viewer-management-document-reports.js
Shared filter projection site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-subscope-report-filter.js

Verification Reference

The primary focused checks are:

python -m pytest \
  docs-viewer/tests/python/test_docs_scope_config.py \
  docs-viewer/tests/python/test_build_docs_subscopes.py \
  docs-viewer/tests/python/test_docs_viewer_public_runtime_boundaries.py -q

python docs-viewer/tests/smoke/docs_viewer_subscope_report_modules.py \
  --site-root .

python admin-app/commands/run_checks.py --profile docs-viewer-smoke

Use an isolated writable DOTLINEFORM_PROJECTS_BASE_DIR when a focused test imports scope config or writes generated external-local data. After source changes, rebuild the affected document/search projection and finish with git diff --check plus a bounded diff review.
